# Vyre

> Vyre is the agentic command center for AI-native teams. Our mission is to help every professional services team become AI-native. People and agents share chats, records, tasks, files and automations (Flows) on a server the team owns, and anything that leaves the team waits for a person's yes. Open source (Apache 2.0), self-hosted, any model: Claude, Codex, Grok and OpenRouter through your own subscriptions or keys. Reach it from the Vyre app on a Mac, on Windows, on a phone, or in a browser.

Current release: 0.5.0. Site: https://vyre.run. Source: https://github.com/vyre-ai/vyre. Licence: Apache 2.0. Vyre is free; you pay your AI providers directly.

## Start here
- [Home](https://vyre.run/): what Vyre is and what it does
- [Get started](https://vyre.run/start/): the steps, from the Vyre app to pairing your server
- [Architecture](https://vyre.run/architecture/): how Vyre is built, on one page: layers, how a call flows, how an agent's turn runs, the Gate
- [Direction](https://vyre.run/direction/): where Vyre is going (direction, not a promise of dates)
- [Privacy](https://vyre.run/privacy/): what Vyre knows about you, which is almost nothing

## Compare
- [Compare Vyre with other tools](https://vyre.run/compare/): how Vyre fits next to automation tools, work management tools, AI assistants and practice software
- [Vyre and automation tools: Zapier, Make and n8n](https://vyre.run/compare/automation-tools/): How Vyre’s approach compares with Zapier, Make and n8n: where app-to-app automation is strong, where Vyre differs, and how the two work together.
- [Vyre and work management tools: Notion, ClickUp, Asana, Monday](https://vyre.run/compare/work-management/): How Vyre compares with Notion, ClickUp, Asana and Monday: what planning tools do well, how Vyre adds agents as members who take tasks, and how to use both.
- [Vyre and AI assistants: team workspaces and agent platforms](https://vyre.run/compare/ai-assistants/): How Vyre compares with team AI assistants such as ChatGPT team workspaces and Claude for teams, and with agent builders: what each does well and how they combine.
- [Vyre with practice software and CRMs: Clio, Karbon, HubSpot](https://vyre.run/compare/practice-software/): Use Clio, Karbon, HubSpot or a similar suite with Vyre: the suite stays your system of record, and Vyre gives your people and agents a place to do the work around it.
- [Vyre and Zapier: works with it, and where Vyre replaces parts of it](https://vyre.run/compare/zapier/): How Vyre works with Zapier today, which parts of the job Vyre does natively, and why that helps a team with fewer tools.

## Devices
- [Mac: Vyre](https://vyre.run/mac/): the Vyre app in its own window
- [Windows: Vyre](https://vyre.run/windows/): tray app with an Alt+Space panel
- [Linux server](https://vyre.run/linux/): where Vyre runs
- [Phone](https://vyre.run/phone/): the Vyre app, sideloaded on Android (APK) or iPhone (Xcode)

## Machine-readable
- [llms-full.txt](https://vyre.run/llms-full.txt): the same content in full
- [agents.md](https://vyre.run/agents.md): guidance for AI agents that install or operate Vyre
- [sitemap.xml](https://vyre.run/sitemap.xml)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/vyre-ai/vyre)
- [Map your business onto Vyre](https://github.com/vyre-ai/vyre/blob/main/docs/for-agents/MAP-YOUR-BUSINESS.md): a method an AI agent follows to turn a business into members, records, Flows, agents and Gate rules
